newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia court allows suit against UN envoy-papers.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia court allows suit against UN envoy-papers.

text.p: The Malaysian High Court has allowed a defamation suit against a United Nations envoy to proceed, saying he was not absolutely protected by immunity, local newspapers reported on Sunday.
U.N. Special Rapporteur on the Independence of Judges and Lawyers, Param Cumaraswamy had sought to halt a suit filed by two Malaysian companies against him in December.
The case has drawn international attention.

But Judicial Commissioner Zainun Ali on Saturday dismissed with costs Param's application to strike out the 60 million ringgit ($23.8 million) suit by MBf Capital Bhd and MBf Northern Securities Sdn Bhd, the New Sunday Times said.

The financial firms claimed in their suit that Param had defamed them in an article published in the November 1995 issue of the International Commercial Litigation magazine, a London-based publication.
In the article, Param was quoted as saying he was investigating complaints that businessmen were manipulating the Malaysian judicial system.
The companies claimed that Param had spoken to a staff writer of the magazine on matters concerning the plaintiffs and their business.
Zainun ordered Param to file and serve his defence within 14 days, but said he was at liberty to cite evidence at the trial to support his claim of immunity.
"All I am deciding for the moment is that on the evidence before me I have jurisdiction to hear this application," she was reported as saying in her 40-page written judgement by New Sunday Times.
"If at the end of the trial, I come to the conclusion that immunity attaches to Param, he may succeed at that stage," she added.
Param could not be immediately contacted for comment.

In a statement received by Reuters late on Saturday, the Geneva-based Centre for the Independence of Judges and Lawyers (CIJL) called on U.N. secretary-general Kofi Annan to immediately bring the case of Param's immunity before the International Court of Justice.
"The Court has assumed jurisdiction over a matter which must be decided by the International Court of Justice," the statement said.
U.N. experts on special missions are granted privileges and immunities for the independent exercise of their functions under an article in the 1946 U.N. convention.

The International Bar Association which represents 2.5 million lawyers worldwide, in January said the libel action against Param contradicted the immunity granted U.N. experts and urged the Malaysian government to protect him.
